title: MLX streams: preserve producer-consumer dependency ordering
summary: The pinned evaluation path uses fences within one evaluation and unfinished events across asynchronous evaluations; a device label alone does not identify the stream dependency.

software: ml-explore/mlx at bff10220c742907f0c68e55ff174aaea56f74e3d; later revisions require reinspection
conditions: Actual backend, streams, shapes/dtypes and evaluation boundary are recorded.
CPU, Metal and CUDA source paths are distinguished; discovery or catalog placement is not runtime qualification.

claims.description: Dependency collection records stream differences and tracks device switches separately. Consumers wait on a same-evaluation fence or an unfinished event from a different stream before primitive dispatch.
synchronize(Stream) selects one stream; the no-argument overload selects the default stream of the default device.

downstream_impact: An InferRSI transfer hypothesis for a matching MLX workload; no implicit vLLM, MLX-LM or other engine compatibility is claimed.
recommendations: Record producer and consumer streams and preserve the existing fence/event path before changing stream placement.
validation_plan: On a separately authorized matching backend, vary same-stream and cross-stream producer-consumer placement with identical inputs and check outputs after the declared completion boundary.
limitations: Ordering a consumer does not itself prove a host-completion wait or permission to release its storage.
CPU/Metal/CUDA implementations require separate execution qualification; this source observation establishes neither cross-device compatibility nor throughput.
